title: Salvation: how are we saved?
opening_question: What does the Bible say about being saved: what we are saved from, what God has done, what we are to do, and whether we can be sure? Read every side the text shows, also the verses Christians read in different ways, and let the text speak.

steps.question: What does Paul say about all people, and what are the wages of sin? What does Isaiah say we have done like sheep?

facts.text: "sin" is hamartia. Strong's: "a sin (properly abstract)". The verb behind it means to miss the mark.
Romans 6:23 sets two things side by side: wages, which are earned, and a gift, which is not: "the gift of God is eternal life".

steps.question: What did God give, and why? When did Christ die for us, and by whom alone can we be saved?

facts.text: God did not wait for us to improve: "while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us".
Peter before the council: "there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved".
"mediator" is mesites, one who stands in the middle. Paul says there is "one mediator between God and men".

steps.question: What is grace? How does Paul say we are saved, and what does he say it is not of?

facts.text: "grace" is charis: favour that is given, not earned. "it is the gift of God", "Not of works, lest any man should boast".
Titus 3:5 says the same from another side: "Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us".

steps.question: What did the jailer ask Paul and Silas, and what did they answer? What does Paul say about the mouth and the heart?

facts.text: The jailer asked the plainest question in the Bible: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"
Paul quotes Joel: "whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved".

steps.question: What did Peter tell the crowd at Pentecost to do? What do these verses say about repentance and baptism, and what did Jesus promise the thief on the cross?

facts.text: Christians read the place of baptism in different ways: some see it as the outward sign of a salvation already received, others as part of how God saves. Read these verses side by side.
The thief on the cross was not baptized, yet Jesus told him: "To day shalt thou be with me in paradise".
Mark 16:9-20 is missing from some of the oldest Greek copies of Mark. Many Bibles print it with a note.

steps.question: What did Jesus tell Nicodemus? What does Paul say happens to anyone who is in Christ?

facts.text: "again" is anothen. Strong's gives both "from above" and "anew". Nicodemus heard "again" and asked how a man can be born "when he is old".
"if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new".

steps.question: Can we know we have eternal life? What does John say, what does Jesus say of His sheep, and what does Paul say about condemnation?

facts.text: John wrote "that ye may know that ye have eternal life". The word is know, not hope.
Of His sheep Jesus says: "neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand".

steps.question: What do these verses say about enduring to the end and about falling away? Read them next to the verses about assurance.

facts.text: Christians read assurance and these warnings together in different ways. Some teach that a true believer cannot be lost and the warnings keep him; others, among them the Wesleyan churches, teach that a believer can fall away. The text gives both, and many read them as meant to be held together.
Paul puts both in one sentence: "work out your own salvation with fear and trembling", and "it is God which worketh in you".

steps.question: Paul says we are justified by faith without the deeds of the law; James says by works, and not by faith only. Read them side by side. What does Ephesians 2:10 add?

facts.text: Both use "justified" (dikaioo). Paul is speaking against works of the law as a way to be accepted; James against a faith that does nothing. Both point to Abraham.
Ephesians 2:10 follows straight after "Not of works": "we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works".

steps.question: Whom does God want to be saved? What does He say about the death of the wicked, and who stands before the throne at the end?

facts.text: God "will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth".
"I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live".
John sees "a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues".

steps.question: Living it out: when is the day of salvation? How shall people hear, and how are we to give an answer for the hope in us?

facts.text: "behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation".
Peter asks for an answer given "with meekness and fear".

"while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us"

"Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved"
